title: Sections over the point of constructible complexes have finite cohomology
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\neq p$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\geq1$; put $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\Gamma(s,-)$ be sections over the final object of $s_{\mathrm{proet}}$, applied termwise to complexes, which is defined on derived categories by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact].

1. For $K\in D^b_c(s,A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility], $\Gamma(s,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A_{E,n})$ [def-weil-point-finite-cohomology-complexes].
2. For $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], regard $\Gamma(s,K)$ as a complex of $\mathcal O_E$-modules through the canonical map $\mathcal O_E=\varprojlim_nA_{E,n}\to\Gamma(s,\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s})$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Then $\Gamma(s,K)\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-point-fg-complete-complexes].
3. For $K\in D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$, $\Gamma(s,K)\otimes_{\mathcal O_E}E\in D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ [def-weil-point-fd-complexes] (termwise tensor product; $E$ is flat over $\mathcal O_E$).

source.place: the assertion that evaluation at the geometric point lands in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}$, $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}$

proof.text:
First $A_{E,n}$ is finite: by the coefficient DVR statement, $\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)$ is finite; choose a finite set $R\subset\mathcal O_E$ of residue representatives. Repeatedly write $x=r_0+\varpi_E x_1$, $x_1=r_1+\varpi_E x_2$, and so on, with $r_j\in R$. Modulo $\varpi_E^n$, every $x$ is therefore represented by $\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}r_j\varpi_E^j$, so at most $|R|^n$ classes occur. For clause (1), take $F=\mathcal H^i(K)$. By finite-torsion constructibility, only finitely many such sheaves are nonzero and each is intrinsically constructible. The finite-ring constructible-sheaf origin theorem supplies a constructible etale $A_{E,n}$-module sheaf $G$ with $F\simeq
u_s^*G$. On $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ any nonempty locally closed subscheme is $s$ itself: an open subset containing its sole point is all of $s$, and a nonzero quotient of its field $k$ is $k$. Thus the etale constructibility definition and the finite-locally-constant module-values theorem show that $G_{\mathrm{id}_s}$ is finite. The algebraically closed etale-point theorem identifies this stalk with $G(s)$. The comparison unit, evaluated at the final etale object, gives $G(s)\simeq(
u_{s,*}
u_s^*G)(s)=(
u_s^*G)(s)=F(s)$, where the equality is the definition of comparison direct image. Exactness of pro-etale sections gives $H^i(\Gamma(s,K))=F(s)$. These are finite and vanish outside the finite cohomological support of $K$, proving (1).

source.place: finite constructible etale origin; algebraically closed point; this argument realizes clause (1) of the blueprint evaluation assertion

proof.text: For the integral clauses put $A=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$ and $I=(\pi)$. The coefficient lemmas give that $A$ is a discrete valuation ring with finite residue field, that $E$ is complete for its nonarchimedean absolute value, and that $0<|\pi|_E<1$. In particular $A$ is Noetherian, since each ideal is principal. We also have $A\simeq\varprojlim_n A/\pi^n$: choose lifts $x_n\in A$ of compatible residues. For $m\geq n$, $x_m-x_n\in\pi^nA$, hence $|x_m-x_n|_E\leq|\pi|_E^n\to0$. Completeness gives a limit $x\in E$; the ultrametric inequality gives $|x|_E\leq1$ and $|x-x_n|_E\leq|\pi|_E^n$, so $x\in A$ has all the prescribed residues. Here $\pi^nA=\{y\in E:|y|_E\leq|\pi|_E^n\}$ follows by dividing by $\pi^n$. Injectivity follows because $|x|_E\leq|\pi|_E^n$ for all $n$ forces $x=0$. This verifies the ring-completeness hypothesis needed below.

source.place: coefficient datum; elementary completeness argument from the three cited coefficient statements

proof.text: Let $K\in D^b_c(s,A)$ and let $K_n$ denote its derived reductions, regarded as completed-coefficient module complexes by restriction of scalars. Put $M=\Gamma(s,K)$ and $M_n=\Gamma(s,K_n)$, viewed as $A$-complexes through the canonical coefficient maps. Choose the interval $[r,t]$ containing the cohomological supports of every $K_n$, as required by the integral constructibility definition. Clause (1) and exact sections show that all $M_n$ have finite cohomology in that same interval. The sheaf-derived completeness definition supplies the Roos triangle $K\to\prod_nK_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nK_n\to K[1]$. Countable products of completed-coefficient sheaves are exact and sectionwise, so the derived product theorem represents these products by termwise products. Exact sections preserve this triangle, its products and the transition map, giving $M\to\prod_nM_n\xrightarrow{1-s}\prod_nM_n\to M[1]$ in $D(A)$. In the module category, countable products are exact: kernels and images are coordinatewise, and a product of surjections is surjective by choosing preimages coordinatewise. Thus the same derived product theorem gives $H^i(\prod_nM_n)=\prod_nH^i(M_n)$. The long exact sequence of the displayed triangle shows $H^i(M)=0$ for $i<r$ or $i>t+1$. Moreover, for any $f\in I$ and any $n$, $f^n$ kills $M_n$, since the latter is an $A/\pi^n$-complex. The nilpotent-torsion derived-limit theorem therefore makes $M$ derived $I$-complete as an $A$-complex. Neither transition-surjectivity on cohomology nor a normalized tower over the quotient rings is used here.

source.place: Tag 091W, lemma-naive-derived-completion; Roos triangle and elementary cohomological bounds from products

proof.text: Write $B=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,s}$. The two-term free $A$-complex $[A\xrightarrow{\pi}A]$, in degrees $[-1,0]$, resolves $A/\pi$, because $A$ is a domain and $\pi\ne0$. The completed-constant-sheaf reduction theorem, applied to this finite free resolution, says that $Q=[B\xrightarrow{\pi}B]\to(A/\pi)_s$ is a quasi-isomorphism. Take a K-flat resolution $P\to K$ as allowed in the derived-reduction definition. Tensoring this quasi-isomorphism with $P$ stays a quasi-isomorphism by the K-flat definition (its cone is the tensor of $P$ with an acyclic cone). But $P\otimes_BQ$ is the cone of $\pi:P\to P$. Thus after restriction of scalars there is a distinguished triangle $K\xrightarrow{\pi}K\to K_1\to K[1]$. Applying exact sections gives the triangle $M\xrightarrow{\pi}M\to M_1\to M[1]$ in $D(A)$. Its long exact sequence induces an injection $H^i(M)/\pi H^i(M)\hookrightarrow H^i(M_1)$ for every $i$, so this quotient is a finite set by step 1, and hence is finitely generated over $A/\pi$ (its finitely many elements form a generating set). This argument only needs the underlying $A$-linear cone triangle; it makes no assertion about derived reduction over $A/\pi^{n+1}$.

source.place: Tag 093M, lemma-completion-flat, finite free resolution clause; K-flat computation of the principal reduction

proof.text: Each cohomology module $N=H^i(M)$ is derived $I$-complete. Indeed, for $f\in I$, completeness of $M$ says that the fibre of $1-s_f:\prod_{j\geq1}M\to\prod_{j\geq1}M$ is zero, where $s_f$ is the shift with transitions multiplication by $f$. Hence $1-s_f$ is an isomorphism; on cohomology it is the bijection $1-s_f:\prod_jH^i(M)\to\prod_jH^i(M)$, by the exact-products formula used in step 3. The Roos triangle for the degree-zero module $N$ then has zero cohomology in every degree (its only possible cohomology is the kernel and cokernel of this bijection). Its derived limit is zero, which is precisely derived completeness of $N$. Apply the new general module-finiteness lemma with $A$, $I=(\pi)$ and $N$: step 2 supplies the complete Noetherian ring, this argument supplies derived completeness, and step 4 supplies the finite residue. It follows that every $H^i(M)$ is finitely generated over $A$. Combined with boundedness and derived completeness from step 3 this is exactly $M\in D^b_{\mathrm{fg}}(A)$, proving (2).

source.place: Tag 091P, lemma-hom-from-Af, equivalence (3)-(4) written directly via Roos products; Tag 09BA, lemma-derived-complete-finite

proof.text: Finally $E=A[1/\pi]$: the discrete-valuation coefficient lemma writes every nonzero $x\in E$ as $u\pi^m$ with $u\in A^\times$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, and the inclusion $A\subset E$ is injective. Thus the localization-flatness theorem makes $E$ flat over $A$. By the flat-tensor exactness theorem, termwise tensoring any representing complex of $M$ with $E$ preserves kernels, images and their quotient sequences. Consequently $H^i(M\otimes_AE)\simeq H^i(M)\otimes_AE$ for every $i$. The finitely many generators of $H^i(M)$ span its scalar extension over $E$; the cohomology still vanishes outside the finite interval from step 3. This is the defining condition for $D^b_{\mathrm{fd}}(E)$ and proves (3).
